note: SEVEN SESSIONS, NOT A YEAR. TradingCalendar as data is session S-E (P1 section 6) and there is not one calendar row anywhere in this repository yet. This file exists so the golden fixtures can resolve a session, and it declares a `coverage` interval the loader enforces (L-08) precisely so it cannot quietly be mistaken for the CME year. When S-E lands, this file is DERIVED from the seeded trading_calendar rows rather than maintained beside them: two hand-maintained calendars is the drift class this corpus has found thirteen times.
why_seven: IT HELD FIVE AND FIVE WAS ONE SHORT AT EACH END, WHICH CI-03 REPORTED AS SIX RED FIXTURES RATHER THAN AS A SHORT CALENDAR. A fixture's day stream is not the whole of what the engine asks the calendar for, and the two days added here are the two the ENGINE reaches for outside the stream. BEFORE 2026-11-02: a funded fixture is handed an explicit prior anchored at `account.opened_on` and `advanceDay` refuses a mark that is not strictly after it (INV-14, R-06). So a funded account's open day must be a session that PRECEDES its first mark, and with the calendar starting on 2026-11-02 a five-day funded stream had nowhere to be opened from. 2026-10-30 is that day. AFTER 2026-11-06: R-31 starts the consistency period on the NEXT trading day after the eval passes, and R-32 counts by sequence subtraction; both refuse with the typed `calendar_coverage_miss` when the day they need is outside the slice (ADR-049, and the miss is UNKNOWN rather than false). So a fixture may pass its eval on the last day it trades, but the calendar must still be able to answer for the day after it. 2026-11-09 is that day. Both are the adjacent CME sessions: 2026-10-30 is the Friday before 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-09 is the Monday after 2026-11-06, and no US exchange holiday falls in either gap. THE SEVEN ARE STILL CONTIGUOUS, which is what keeps the loader's synthesized `sequence` (position in this array) equal to the dense calendar index, as `golden-loader/src/calendar.ts` states and as R-02's subtraction requires.
derivation: NOT DERIVED YET, AND THAT IS NOW A CHECKED FACT RATHER THAN A PROMISE IN THE NOTE ABOVE. `CI-06m` asserts what can be asserted about a hand-maintained fixture: that `session_count` and the `sessions` array are two independent statements of one number and agree, that every session falls inside `coverage`, and that no session falls on a weekend. It cannot assert the DAYS are right, because the CME publication has not been transcribed: `packages/db/src/seed/calendars/cme-2026-2028.source.json` carries `holidays: null`, `generate.mjs` refuses it on `source-not-transcribed`, and there is nothing to derive from. The day the founder transcribes it, this file becomes `generated_by` output and `CI-06m`'s second check regenerates and diffs it, which is the pattern `corpus.yml` already uses for generated spans. `status: partial` is what says the derivation has not happened; a fixture that is not `partial` and names no generator is a finding.
